title: What they said at the time

clips.q: No child forgets the first visit to FAO Schwarz.
clips.who: **FAO Inc.**, annual report on Form 10-K, filed May 16, 2003, three weeks after it left its first bankruptcy[^1]

clips.q: I think consumers were spending less on upscale toy retail products.
clips.who: **Maria Weiskott**, Playthings magazine, after the first filing, January 2003[^12]

clips.q: So, FAO, as a company as we know it, will cease to exist.
clips.who: **Carrie Lee**, reporting from the Nasdaq for CNN, December 3, 2003[^15]

clips.q: FAO Schwarz is more than just a toy store.
clips.who: **David E. Shaw**, D. E. Shaw & Co., January 26, 2004[^16]

clips.q: The holidays just wouldn’t be the same without FAO Schwarz.
clips.who: **David E. Shaw**, before the Fifth Avenue store reopened, November 2004[^18]

clips.q: The decision to vacate this space is due to the continuing rising costs of operating a retail location on Fifth Avenue in New York City.
clips.who: **FAO Schwarz** statement, May 15, 2015, as reported by Reuters[^23]

clips.q: For over one hundred and fifty years, FAO has provided a magical experience for children and we hope to keep this tradition alive by crafting fine toys and transformative retail experiences for generations to come.
clips.who: **Kirk McLean**, ThreeSixty Group, to Fortune, October 4, 2016[^26]

clips.q: We are about experiences. That’s what’s different from other toy stores.
clips.who: **David Niggli**, chief merchandising officer, to the Associated Press, November 2018[^29]
